signals.brief_en:
Title: Akhilvallala1/veil
A privacy firewall for computer-use AI agents. Muse Wonder can only view veiled screens, while the open-weight Muse Glimmer and SAM 3.1 monitor the raw pixel data. Demonstrated at the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026. The system aims to limit data exposure for AI assistants, but its effectiveness against sophisticated side‑channel analysis remains unproven.

signals.title: @RodmanAi: 10 GitHub Repos Using AI to Turn Satellite Images Into Real-World Insights What if you could identify forests, map roads, detect buildings,
signals.content: 10 GitHub Repos Using AI to Turn Satellite Images Into Real-World Insights What if you could identify forests, map roads, detect buildings, and monitor floods using nothing but satellite imagery and AI? That's exactly what these open-source projects are helping developers and researchers do. Here are 10 repositories worth exploring: 1. TorchGeo A powerful toolkit for training deep learning models on geospatial data and satellite imagery. https://t.co/j5Ki7P9hhw 2. Segment Anything Use prompt-based segmentation to identify objects and regions in images. https://t.co/PzesDRI5nP 3. Clay Explore foundation models built specifically for Earth observation and geospatial intelligence. https://t.co/nGRFpFrip8 4. Prithvi NASA's geospatial AI models for applications like flood mapping, land cover analysis, and environmental monitoring. https://t.co/xVhgFyuzxC 5. SAMGeo Bring promptable image segmentation into satellite and geospatial analysis workflows. https://t.co/RksOm4MLjk 6. eo-learn Create reusable pipelines for processing satellite imagery and detecting changes across landscapes. https://t.co/43n8goucJd 7. Raster Vision Build computer vision pipelines for classifying images and detecting geographic features. https://t.co/xIR9oIA68v 8. DeepForest Detect individual tree crowns from aerial imagery using deep learning. https://t.co/EburiNo5VK 9. Solaris Develop geospatial computer vision workflows for object detection and image segmentation. https://t.co/w31QisrGMI 10. SpaceNet Access satellite imagery datasets and benchmarks for mapping roads, buildings, and infrastructure. https://t.co/ni3BoHzhC8 The exciting part? These aren't just tools for looking at satellite pictures. They help turn raw imagery into useful information about our changing planet. From tracking deforestation to understanding urban growth, the applications are enormous. Save these repos. The next big AI breakthrough might come from looking down at Earth.

signals.title: AzadKurt/videoworker-mcp
signals.content: FFmpeg for AI agents. Upload local media, process video/audio/images remotely, and download results via MCP.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: AzadKurt/videoworker-mcp
Brief: This open‑source project provides an FFmpeg‑based service that enables AI agents to upload local media files, have video, audio, or image processing performed on a remote server, and retrieve the processed results via the MCP (Media Control Protocol). The tool is designed for integration into autonomous workflows, offering a programmable interface for batch transcoding, filtering, and analysis. Current documentation confirms basic functionality; performance metrics and security assessments are limited, so operational reliability should be validated before deployment in critical systems.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: AzadKurt/videoworker-mcp
الملخص: يوفّر هذا المشروع مفتوح المصدر خدمة تعتمد على FFmpeg تمكّن الوكلاء الذكائيين من رفع ملفات وسائط محلية، وإجراء معالجة للفيديو أو الصوت أو الصور على خادم بعيد، ثم تنزيل النتائج عبر بروتوكول MCP (Media Control Protocol). صُمم الأداة لتُدمج في سير عمل ذاتي، وتقدّم واجهة برمجية للترميز الجماعي، والترشيح، والتحليل. توثيق المشروع يؤكد الوظيفة الأساسية؛ إلا أن مقاييس الأداء وتقييمات الأمان ما زالت محدودة، لذا يُنصح بالتحقق من موثوقية التشغيل قبل الاعتماد في أنظمة حرجة.
